item.text: The central tree is 32% shorter by line count and 33% shorter by character count. Five peripherals add source-backed detail. I also corrected the seed’s unconditional claim about opening a saved view: reopening the active view only stashes state, and camera preservation depends on a supplied viewport. All diagram bounds and edge line references pass the checks.

  "explanation": "The central tree retains the seed's main responsibilities while shrinking from 113 to 77 lines (32%) and from 8655 to 5817 characters (33%). Five peripherals expand revision resolution, command consequences, spatial composition, saved-view lifecycles and transfers. Modular structure is expressed through component boundaries; call sequences show execution; ownership identifies retained state; data dependencies explain checkpoint materialization and reference remapping. Edges attach to the relevant concept lines. Positions use measured text bounds with gaps and no overlaps.

Source grounding: refs uses canvasHistory.ts; cmd uses mappingDocumentController.ts and mappingWorkspace.ts; grid uses lineGrid.ts, mappingGrid.ts and the controller; views uses canvasHistory.ts and canvasView.ts; move uses canvasTransfer.ts and canvasHistoryService.ts. Added details absent from the seed include operation-count limits, stale selection retention, section removal after patches, collision ordering, geometry limits, candidate-update identity checks and shared-content preservation during transfers.

Corrections and qualifications: the seed describes opening a CanvasView as always restoring a fresh checkpoint. canvasHistory.ts:278-288 shows that reopening the active view only stashes state, appending only when the supplied personal view differs; switching preserves the camera only when a viewport is supplied. Saved-view execution belongs to CanvasHistory, while canvasView.ts defines schemas and validation. canvasTransfer.ts:134-159 establishes that moving converts every source edge into a jump, including edges between remaining diagrams.

Only the supplied point, pinned source text and seed were used. Workspace publication is an ownership contract stated in the transfer source; its implementation is outside these inputs. Imported helper internals and browser/server integration were not independently verified.",
